blocks.orig: The Nasikia Mobile Migration Camp is a mobile tented camp that moves through the amazing Serengeti National Park twice a year. From early December to the end of March, it is set up in the Small Marsh of the Ndutu region, an ideal location to observe the zebras and wildebeest of the Great Migration calving. Along with those young animals, predators such as lions, hyenas, jackals, wild dogs, and cheetahs can be spotted. The camp offers 11 safari tents (including one family tent), each made of locally produced canvas with mosquito netting. The ensuite tents have single or double beds, seating, and private patios. Meals are served in the large dining tent set under an acacia tree.
blocks.html: The Nasikia Mobile Migration Camp is a tented camp on the move: twice a year it relocates within the amazing Serengeti National Park. From early December until late March you find it in the Ndutu region, in the Small Marsh, which is perfectly placed for seeing the zebras and wildebeest of the Great Migration have their young. Alongside the newborns, predators like cheetahs, wild dogs, jackals, hyenas and lions can be seen. The camp has 11 safari tents, one of which is a family tent, all made of canvas produced locally and fitted with mosquito netting. Inside each ensuite tent are single or double beds, a place to sit and a private patio. You eat in the big dining tent under an acacia tree.
